findings.description: [expert] This filter only changes receipts written after the fix. Receipts already on disk are never pruned, and the anchor check reads every cycle, so any existing receipt that still contains a sentinel INFRA anchor will continue to fail attestation forever. The comment at lines 112-113 acknowledges the permanent failure mode, but the fix does not remediate or ignore those existing receipts; add a verifier-side tolerance for non-path sentinels or a one-time migration/cleanup.

[expert] Filtering by source label ('INFRA') is broader than the stated problem. If an INFRA finding ever carries a real file path rather than a sentinel, this silently drops its anchor and weakens the audit trail. The predicate should test whether the path is a sentinel (e.g. starts with '<' or is in an explicit sentinel set), not whether the finding source is INFRA.

[adversarial] Filtering INFRA findings out of anchors removes the stale sentinel block, but it leaves no per-pass proof that a failed pass actually read the diff. Coverage is computed per cycle, not per receipt: in test_receipt_writer_output_passes_verify, each pass receipt individually covers only ~20-26% of the 80-line diff, yet verify passes when the three passes are unioned. Therefore a cycle whose qodo pass returns only an INFRA finding can still pass if the other two passes cover >=60% of a small diff. The new test only uses an 80-line diff where two passes produce 42/80 (<60%), so it misses this attestation bypass.

[adversarial] The new backend-failure tests call run_verify without diff_text, so they exercise the legacy branch, not the hardened diff_text path used in production. The asserted 'coverage' failure and the INFRA-anchor filtering behavior are not verified for the hardened branch, so a regression specific to that path would not be caught by these tests.
